business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Operations in Customs Free Trade Zones

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus) — ratified and in force for Samoa
World Trade Organization (WTO) membership — Samoa acceded in 2012
Samoa Agreement (EU-ACP partnership, successor to the Cotonou Agreement)

No dedicated Samoa-China Bilateral Investment Treaty or Double Taxation Agreement is confirmed in force; treaty benefits must be verified on a case-by-case basis for the proposed free trade zone bonded depot operation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended; Money Laundering Prevention Regulations 2008; Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit Beneficial Ownership and Customer Due Diligence Guidelines; applicable Customs and Free Trade Zone licensing statutes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of passport (biographic page and signature page) for each proposed director, shareholder, secretary, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document holder's country of origin; legalized by the competent foreign affairs authority or Samoan diplomatic/consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months, showing the proposed principal's full name and address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider; notarized and legalized as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming client due diligence status, account relationship length, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal commercial bank of the shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner; bank officer signature notarized and legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or corporate registry extract when the applicant or UBO is a legal entity, showing registered address, directors, shareholders, and beneficial ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or licensed corporate agent of the upstream entity; authenticated for Samoa filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and the licensed bonded depot manager against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated domestic list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists, and major international debarment databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Confirmed sanctions or adverse AML matches require immediate suspension of incorporation until cleared by the Samoa FIU or relevant regulator.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia — Official Company Name Search and Reservation Desk
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Latin script (English or Samoan). Non-Latin script such as Chinese is permitted only as a secondary registered name after a Registrar-approved Romanized transliteration. The constitutional/charter may be drafted in Chinese, but a certified English or Samoan translation must accompany the filing for public record and statutory enforcement.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Samoa (where use would imply government or public authority affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for a further 30 days by paying the prescribed extension fee to MCIL before expiry. On rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days, stating the legal grounds for reversal and providing a revised name proposal if appropriate. The appeal must be submitted using the registry's prescribed form and accompanied by the original rejection notice. If the word falls within a prohibited or sensitive category, the applicant must first obtain written ministerial approval from the relevant sector regulator; the appeal will otherwise fail and a fresh name reservation will be required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the physical bonded depot operation. The International Company must maintain a statutory registered office at the licensed registered agent's street address in Samoa for legal service of process; however, the free trade zone bonded warehouse must be a physical, staffed, customs-approved facility within a designated free trade zone. A virtual office may not substitute for the licensed warehouse or satisfy the customs supervision and physical inspection requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated 75% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first operating year. Samoa Customs and free trade zone regulators conduct periodic and intelligence-led on-site inspections of bonded warehouses to verify inventory, records, customs seals, and physical security.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and statutory name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Companies Registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International Company incorporation and registry stamp charges (standard authorized capital)
Registered office and licensed registered agent service — first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Samoa international company administration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register setup, customer due diligence file, and PEP/sanctions vetting for three natural-person principals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / Samoa FIU-supervised reporting entity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Enhanced due diligence schedule per principal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille or consular legalization of passport, proof of address, and bank reference documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, competent foreign affairs authority, and Samoan diplomatic/consular mission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter procurement and banker's professional introduction for three principals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing banking charge and interviewer fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed customs broker fee for free trade zone bonded depot license application dossier and customs supervision plan
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional service fee benchmark for Samoa customs licensing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Samoa Customs applicability assessment, tariff classification ruling, and free trade zone compliance consultation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoa Customs / Ministry of Customs and Revenue / external customs law counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government advisory fee and professional legal fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 5, 7 and 9 (incorporation, registered office and registered agent); Free Trade Zones Act (Samoa) and Customs Act 1977, as amended, for bonded depot licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation (together with Memorandum and Articles of Association)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement; the subscriber may subscribe for one share of any stated value
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the first resolution of the Board of Directors of [Company Name] (the 'Company'), that: (1) the Company subscribes to and adopts the Memorandum and Articles of Association as lodged with the Registrar of International Companies; (2) one fully paid ordinary share shall be allotted to the initial subscriber; (3) the registered office at [Address], Apia, Samoa, is adopted and [Registered Agent] is appointed as registered agent; (4) [Name] is appointed Director, [Name] Company Secretary, and [Name] authorised signatory for customs and free trade zone licensing; and (5) the Directors are authorised to open bank accounts and execute all documents necessary to obtain business, FTZ and bonded warehouse licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); lodged via licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to submit a name reservation request to the Registrar of International Companies with up to three proposed corporate names ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The Registrar screens for identical or deceptively similar names on the International Companies register. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identification documents (passport and proof of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the registered agent re-files with alternative names within 3 business days; written reasons may be requested from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association, subscriber statement, and consents of the first director and secretary. The sole subscriber executes the charter documents. The registered office address in Samoa and the registered agent's appointment are stated in the application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective clauses are amended and re-executed before lodgment; no additional state fee for internal corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Form 1 Application for Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form 1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles and pays the government filing fee. The registered agent certifies compliance with the International Companies Act 1987.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition letter, corrections are resubmitted within 14 days; an extension may be requested in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered agent collects the certificate and confirms the registration number and date of incorporation; thereafter the company may open bank accounts and enter into contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the certificate are corrected by a formal rectification request to the Registrar; a proportionate fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the charter documents, allot the initial share, confirm the registered office and registered agent, and authorise the opening of bank accounts. Minutes are signed and filed in the registered office records.
required_dossiers: Share subscription and letter of allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural defects are cured by a ratifying board resolution; an indemnity may be given to the registered agent if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Free Trade Zone Enterprise Licence Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Trade, Commerce and Industry Division (Free Trade Zone Authority functions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for designation as a Free Trade Zone Enterprise (bonded depot operator) with the Certificate of Incorporation, the FTZ site lease or sub-lease, a warehouse operations plan, and a financial standing statement. The licence imposes customs control, record-keeping and reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: FTZ site lease or sub-lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A rejected application may be reconsidered by the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour, or re-filed with a revised operations plan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bonded Warehouse Licence and Customs Bond Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge an application for a bonded warehouse licence under the Customs Act 1977 (as amended) for the FTZ depot site. Submit the site plan, inventory control system description, security arrangements, and execute a customs bond or bank guarantee. Customs officials inspect the premises before approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If customs refuses due to premises or security deficiencies, remedy the stated deficiencies and submit a fresh application; a written objection may be lodged with the Commissioner of Customs within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Trade, Commerce and Industry Division, in conjunction with the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) Customs Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Free Trade Zone Enterprise Licence and Bonded Warehouse Licence (customs-managed depot)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 (Development Consent with EIA Report) for new depot construction; Category 3 (Environmental Registration) for existing buildings converted to bonded storage
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Effluent discharge must comply with water quality standards issued under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; VOC emissions limited to permissible ambient air thresholds; solid waste segregated and handled in accordance with the Waste Management Act 2004

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the warehouse premises from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA); workplace clearance under occupational safety and health norms of the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013; structural load certification for racking and storage areas issued by a registered engineer and accepted by the MCIL Building Division

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (Office of the Commissioner of Revenue), Apia, Samoa; official taxpayer e-Services/e-Filing portal operated by the Ministry for Revenue (MRE e-Services). Samoa Customs Service, administered within the revenue portfolio, handles customs export clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 2012 through the Samoa Companies Registry (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour), obtaining a Certificate of Incorporation and a Registered Agent Certificate. Step 2: Submit Form IR-CR/2 (Application for Tax Identification Number) to the Ministry for Revenue together with the certificate of incorporation, registered agent/office details, director and shareholder particulars, and beneficial owner identification. Step 3: If the IC will make taxable VAGST supplies exceeding the threshold in the next 12 months, file Form VAGST-R (VAGST Registration Application) with projected turnover, business description, and any free trade zone or bonded warehouse licence; the Commissioner will issue a VAGST registration number. Step 4: Obtain a Free Trade Zone licence under the Free Trade Zones Act 2010 and a bonded warehouse approval from Samoa Customs before conducting duty-suspended or zero-rated depot operations. Step 5: A foreign-owned IC transacting wholly offshore is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax and VAGST but must still procure a TIN for customs, administrative, and annual government fee compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable. Samoa does not administer a US-style check-the-box election, partnership classification, or hybrid-mismatch elective regime. A Samoa IC is classified by statute as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 2012, and free trade zone/bonded depot operators benefit from the statutory exemption and zero-rating rules of the Free Trade Zones Act 2010 and the VAGST Act 2008. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule in the Income Tax Ordinance 2015 and the Tax Administration Act 2012 may recharacterize abusive classification or mismatch arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) - Samoa's national VAT-style consumption tax governed by the VAGST Act 2008 and VAGST Regulations, supplemented by customs tariff and excise legislation for imports and specified goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 50,000 (Samoan Tala) of taxable supplies in the preceding or prospective 12-month period; a person making or likely to make taxable supplies exceeding WST 50,000 must register for VAGST. Foreign entities and non-residents carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa, including bonded warehouse or free trade zone operations with a local supply nexus, are subject to the same threshold unless an express statutory exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate is currently legislated in Samoa. VAGST tax invoices must include prescribed particulars (serial number, tax identification numbers, supplier and recipient details, date, and VAGST-exclusive/inclusive pricing) and be retained for seven years. The Ministry for Revenue continues to digitalize taxpayer e-filing but does not require government pre-clearance or API submission of invoices. Bonded depot operators must nevertheless maintain electronic customs-linked stock and transfer records evidencing goods movement into and out of the free trade zone.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act 2008, a 0% rate applies to (a) goods physically exported from Samoa by the supplier within a prescribed timeframe and substantiated by customs export documentation; (b) services supplied to non-residents or for consumption wholly outside Samoa, including bonded warehouse handling, storage, and logistics services performed for non-resident principals in respect of goods destined for export; and (c) supplies made between licensed free trade zone operators while goods remain in bond or customs suspension. The exporter must retain evidence of physical export, maintain valid VAGST registration, and ensure export proceeds are received into Samoa within the statutory FX repatriation deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs electronic export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the receiving Samoan bank confirming export proceeds repatriation
VAGST export tax invoice showing the 0% rate or zero-rating statement with both supplier and recipient TINs
Bonded Warehouse Removal / Transit Entry evidencing customs-authorized transfer from the free trade zone depot to the export conveyance
Free Trade Zone Licence and warehouse goods in/out register supporting the bonded movement trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims and claw back VAGST at 15% plus statutory shortfall penalties where physical export, export documentation, or FX repatriation within 180 days is not substantiated. Fraudulent zero-rating, forged customs declarations, or false export certifications attract: (i) tax shortfall penalties of up to 150% for intentional or reckless non-compliance under the Tax Administration Act 2012; (ii) monthly late-payment penalties on assessed tax; (iii) criminal fines and imprisonment of up to three years for directors or officers involved in fraudulent evasion; and (iv) revocation of bonded warehouse and free trade zone licences together with deregistration of VAGST privilege. Retrospective assessments may extend beyond standard time limits where evasion or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — the national monetary authority and sole exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; all licensed commercial banks operate as CBS-licensed authorised foreign-exchange dealers, exercising delegated approval thresholds with CBS retaining jurisdiction over capital-account and large-value applications.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST), managed by the CBS against a trade-weighted basket of partner currencies (USD, AUD, NZD, EUR, JPY), is not freely convertible. Current-account payments (imports, freight, insurance, agency fees) are approved routinely by authorised dealer banks on documentary evidence. Capital-account transactions — inbound equity capitalisation, shareholder loans, dividends, liquidation or branch remittances, and offshore loan repayments — require prior CBS exchange-control approval or an explicit dealer-bank delegated limit, plus, where applicable, a Foreign Investment Certificate under the Foreign Investment Act 2020 (unless a written legal exemption confirms that FTZ offshore warehousing falls outside the foreign-investment activity definition). For an International Company, dividend remittances are income-tax-exempt at source but operationally must clear CBS outward-remittance review supported by audited retained-earnings evidence. Practical hurdles: (i) correspondent-bank de-risking limiting USD/AUD clearing into Apia; (ii) CBS processing windows of 2–5 business days for non-automatic approvals; (iii) strict documentary back-up for every capital movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Exchange Control Act 1976 and CBS policy instruments require all export and re-export proceeds, including sales of bonded Free Trade Zone inventory, to be repatriated to Samoa within 90 days of shipment and sold (surrendered) to an authorised dealer bank in WST, unless the CBS has granted an exemption permitting retention in a Samoan foreign-currency account or an approved offshore account. The statutory surrender ratio for a standard bonded/reexport operator is 100% of the net foreign-currency proceeds. Compliance evidence includes the customs declaration, bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and bank credit advice, retained for at least five years for CBS/FIU audit; any deviation requires pre-approval through the CBS outward-remittance approval process, and non-compliant proceeds are recoverable by the CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
National Bank of Samoa Limited (state-owned retail bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution or digital-bank licensing category; the Banking Ordinance 2000 and CBS licensing rules do not recognise offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer) as authorised dealers. Such EMIs cannot hold WST clearing accounts, cannot issue Samoan clearing codes, and routing payments through them may breach the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018. Feasible workaround: maintain a Tier-1 Samoan dealer bank as the sole licensed settlement point and use an overseas EMI only for pre-settlement aggregation outside Samoa, forwarding funds to the Samoan account by SWIFT MT103.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote document-only account opening is not available for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced FTZ bonded-depot operator. Each Tier-1 bank requires a live KYC interview — in person at the Apia branch or by bank-approved secure video call — with each director and every ultimate beneficial owner. UBOs must present or certify passports and proof of address; the corporate pack (certificate of incorporation, SIFA certificate of good standing, register of directors and shareholders, board resolution, and registered-agent letter) must be delivered by courier as original or certified/apostilled copies. BSP and ANZ accept video-interview onboarding where the introducer is a SIFA-licensed registered agent or a regulated Apia law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership structure — nominee shareholders, trust-held IC shares, multi-layer foreign holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; register of directors, shareholders and UBOs; chain-of-title organisational chart ending at natural persons; trust deed extracts limited to UBO identification; registered-agent client-due-diligence file from the SIFA-licensed agent

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Free-trade-zone / bonded-warehouse typology — customs-fraud, tariff-evasion or trade-based money-laundering profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FTZ enterprise licence under the Free Trade Zones Act 2000; customs bonded-warehouse licence under the Customs Management Act 2015; executed FTZ lease or occupancy agreement; warehouse operational plan with inventory ledger and stock-control system; sample customs entries and re-export declarations; third-party logistics and security contracts; management accounts demonstrating real trade economics

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection without visible source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month bank statements of the remitting account; signed source-of-wealth declaration by each UBO; board resolution approving the equity injection; underlying commercial contract or pro-forma invoice for the first bonded-stock purchase; Foreign Investment Certificate or legal-exemption opinion; CBS inward-investment notification form

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions-list or adverse-media flags on Chinese-speaking beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Date-of-birth, nationality and full-name screening pack against UN, OFAC, DFAT and EU sanctions lists; PEP declaration with risk-acceptance memorandum signed by the bank's money-laundering reporting officer; adverse-media mitigation narrative; notarised lawful-source-of-wealth declaration; legal certification from licensed Apia counsel

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency ambiguity — IC claiming full Samoan tax exemption while operating a physical warehouse in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IC certificate of exemption or ruling from the Ministry for Revenue confirming non-resident tax-exempt status under the International Companies Act 2018; legal opinion on the boundary between IC offshore status and FTZ domestic-presence rules; confirmation that no retail or domestic goods are sold into Samoa customs territory; arms-length pricing policy for payments to any related Samoan FTZ service provider

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity and shareholder-loan injections must flow by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank) to the IC's WST or USD account at a CBS-licensed authorised dealer. Use approved CBS SWIFT purpose codes mapped by the dealer bank — inward-investment / equity capitalisation, intercompany loan, and trade-goods codes — accompanied by the bank's inward-remittance advice. Supporting file: board resolution, share subscription or loan agreement, source-of-wealth pack, and Foreign Investment Certificate or legal exemption. Funds originating from China must reflect SAFE-approved outbound ODI equity or trade-in-goods remittance to avoid refusal; the receiving bank will escrow the credit pending CBS reconciliation of the inward-investment notification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 payment orders for supplier settlements, with underlying invoice, packing list and transport document appended electronically. Commercial letters of credit are issued via SWIFT MT700 with a Samoan advising or negotiating bank (BSP or ANZ) and a confirming bank in the supplier's jurisdiction for high-value stock purchases. Domestic WST disbursements (FTZ rent, utilities, wages, customs bonds) clear through the CBS-overseen interbank clearing and RTGS in WST using standard local settlement instruments. Outward capital and high-value trade payments require CBS outward-remittance approval and the re-export certificate from Samoa Customs; the bank matches every outward payment against the surrender discipline on related export proceeds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts (USD/WST, AUD/WST) with a CBS-licensed authorised dealer, available up to 12 months against bona fide commercial trade exposure (bonded-stock purchases or re-export receivables) supported by underlying contracts.
Plain-vanilla FX options (USD/WST) on a discretionary bank-offered basis where the option premium is embedded in the trade contract and the bank holds a CBS hedging mandate.

Cross-currency swaps — technically permissible only with prior written CBS Exchange Control approval and only where linked to a specific financing or trade facility; in practice Samoan banks do not offer WST swaps to ICs, so the de facto hedge is the WST basket peg.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST — not permissible; there is no recognised offshore NDF market for the tala, and any such contract would be an unauthorised exchange-control transaction subject to CBS sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company exempt-status Government License Fee (base band: authorized capital up to US$100,000; US$300 band for US$100,001–US$1,000,000; US$500 band above US$1,000,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies — Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on the anniversary of incorporation; the licensed registered agent remits the fee before the anniversary date; no annual return or accounts are filed with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% on the unpaid annual fee; the Registrar may administratively strike off and dissolve the International Company after 90 days of arrears; restoration requires a Court petition and payment of all arrears, penalties, and restoration charges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Bonded Warehouse / Free Trade Zone Customs Depot license with revalidation of the customs security bond and submission of the annual bonded stock reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Customs and Excise Division — Ministry for Revenue (Free Trade Zone and bonded warehouse licensing unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the license anniversary date specified in the customs license; the renewal application and stock reconciliation return are lodged at least 30 days before expiry; applicable renewal and inspection fees are assessed under the customs tariff and license schedule rather than a fixed statutory USD amount
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating after expiry suspends the bonded status; continued default triggers license revocation, forfeiture or call-out of the customs security bond, restoration of goods to customs control, and re-imposition of duty with penalties for unauthorized bonded warehouse operation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to any Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended 2008); the exemption is unlimited in scope regardless of turnover, assets, or shareholder number; an audit may be triggered only internally (constitutional document, director/shareholder resolution) or by a third party (bank financing, surety of the customs security bond) for this bonded depot operation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Section 174 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended 2008) requires accounting records sufficient to show and explain transactions and to determine the financial position with reasonable accuracy; no IFRS or local GAAP preparation and no filing of accounts with the Registrar are required; IFRS or cash-basis records acceptable to the lender or customs surety may be adopted when statements are prepared voluntarily

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa does not require a public or Registrar-facing UBO return for International Companies; the licensed registered agent maintains the AML/CFT beneficial ownership identification file as the mandatory compliance record. Annually, at the fee-renewal cycle, the agent obtains a signed director/shareholder declaration confirming the current shareholding, share transfers registered during the year, and any UBO changes; the agent updates the UBO and CDD records within 14 days of any notified change, including transfers executed through nominees or trust structures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages (if any security interests exist)
Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' meeting records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–950 per year (licensed Samoa registered agent inclusive of registered office, statutory register custody, UBO/AML record maintenance, and annual fee processing)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit is required; where a voluntary audit is demanded by lenders or the customs bond surety for the bonded depot, a local CPA firm will typically charge USD 4,500–12,000 depending on transaction volume and record quality

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Company (IC) licensed under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) is exempt from income tax on offshore-source income. Income generated purely within the licensed Free Trade Zone / Bonded Depot and derived from non-resident cargo owners is treated as offshore income, producing a zero effective CIT rate. The tax obligation is discharged through the annual IC license fee (statutory range WST 30 to WST 5,000 by reference to authorised capital). Domestic-market sales into the Samoan customs territory are taxable at the headline 27% rate; no other preferential tax holiday applies to the warehousing activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Ministry of Revenue (MoR) Company Income Tax Return Form CIT-R1 submitted electronically via the MoR 'Revenue Online' e-Filing Portal at revenue.gov.ws. An offshore-exempt International Company concurrently files the Registrar of International Companies Annual Return (Form IC-AR) and the MoR Economic Substance Return (Form ESR-IC) through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final CIT return is due within six months after the income year end; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 30 June of the following year. The Commissioner may grant a written extension of up to three months. Quarterly provisional tax instalments fall due on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IC registration number, MoR Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and bonded depot licence expiry date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Samoa-registered IC name exactly as stated on the certificate of incorporation; any change of foreign director must be notified via Form D1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income allocated between 'Offshore/FTZ bonded storage and warehousing services' and 'Domestic customs-territory sales'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income from storage, handling, repacking and transfer of cargo confined to the Free Trade Zone Bonded Depot is declared as non-resident exempt and coded 'Zero-rated'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross storage fees, handling charges, demurrage and ancillary logistics revenue invoiced to cargo owners during the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Samoa-source amounts; invoices rendered to overseas principals for offshore-only logistics are excluded from withholding tax when accompanied by the DTA/offshore exemption schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Customs-bonded inventory purchases, warehouse rent, security, utilities and FTZ administrative permit fees directly attributable to depot operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC claiming the offshore exemption may leave the schedule blank, provided cost records are retained in Samoa for ESR and audit inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and management fees allowable under the Income Tax Act 2015; penalties, speculative reserves and payments to foreign service providers not subjected to 15% withholding where required are disallowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenditure paid to foreign related parties must be supported by a contemporaneous transfer pricing file where the statutory threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover less cost of sales and allowable deductions, before loss carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an FTZ-exempt IC this field is computed at WST 0 where Box 2 shows 100% offshore turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses, limited to a maximum of five years under the Income Tax Act 2015, applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore ICs enter NIL; losses cannot be offset against the domestic-taxed portion of a mixed-activity IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 27% on taxable income less treaty or unilateral foreign tax credits and quarterly provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero-rated for offshore-exempt ICs; any domestic-tax proportion is payable in Samoan Tala through the Revenue Online portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic declaration by a director or the Samoa-licensed registered agent attesting to completeness and accuracy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must have the return countersigned by its Samoa-licensed registered agent; the agent assumes statutory personal liability for knowingly false schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of WST 500 plus a daily surcharge of WST 50, capped at WST 10,000. Late payment triggers a 10% penalty on the outstanding tax plus monthly interest of 2% per month or part-month. Knowingly lodging a false return is a criminal offence punishable by a fine up to WST 100,000, imprisonment up to seven years, and restitution of the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Samoa-resident company to non-resident shareholders. Dividends of an offshore-exempt International Company are outside the WHT charge where the dividend is sourced entirely from FTZ/offshore income. Under the New Zealand-Samoa Double Taxation Agreement, the rate is 15% on portfolio dividends and 5% where the beneficial owner holds directly at least 25% of the paying company's capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) the paying IC obtains a Samoa Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the MoR using Form TRC-COP; (2) the foreign beneficial owner supplies its own TRC and a declaration of beneficial ownership on Form WHT-DTA-15; (3) the MoR is notified through the Revenue Online portal no later than fifteen days before the distribution date; (4) the reduced-rate payment is made and all documentation retained for seven years. Where the shareholder is resident in a non-treaty state, the 15% statutory rate applies unless the IC is in the offshore-exempt class.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 15% on interest paid to non-residents and 15% on royalties paid for the use of depot technology, customs software, branding or racking systems. Under the New Zealand-Samoa DTA, interest and royalties are both reduced to 10% where the beneficial owner is a New Zealand resident. Back-to-back financing through a zero-tax intermediary does not eliminate WHT absent treaty entitlement; the Samoan payor must withhold on each gross remittance and remit the WHT to the MoR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A contemporaneous Samoa Local File is mandatory where aggregate connected-party transactions, including bonded storage fees, handling charges, group management fees and related-party interest, exceed WST 5,000,000 in an income year. A Master File is required where the overseas parent group has consolidated turnover exceeding WST 50,000,000 or where related-party cargo passing through the bonded depot exceeds WST 10,000,000. Below the threshold, a summary transfer pricing declaration (Form TP-IC) must still be filed for any IC with cross-border related-party transactions. All documentation must be in English and produced to the MoR within 30 days of demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa Economic Substance Requirements (2020) apply to every International Company, including the FTZ Bonded Depot activity class. The IC must demonstrate: (i) physical office premises in Samoa; (ii) at least two board meetings per year held in Samoa; (iii) a bank account in Samoa; (iv) adequate employees and core income-generating expenditure in Samoa proportionate to the warehousing logistics activity; and (v) books and records maintained in or accessible from Samoa. An annual Economic Substance Return (ESR-IC) is due within six months from year-end. Failure attracts financial penalties, potential loss of offshore tax-exempt status, deregistration, and automatic exchange of information to the jurisdiction of the ultimate beneficial owner under the multilateral exchange framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating bonded depot turnover, issuing side contracts invoiced outside Samoa, removing cargo without customs recording, or introducing goods into the domestic customs territory without payment of the 27% corporate tax and applicable customs duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil assessment of the full evaded tax, an evader penalty equal to 200% of the tax shortfall where fraud is proved, and daily late-payment interest of 2% per month. Criminal prosecution may impose a fine up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors who signed or caused the false return are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall. The court may issue a departure prohibition order (travel ban) pending settlement, order confiscation of personal assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act, and impose direct custodial sentences on individual wrongdoers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a letterbox free trade zone entity with no physical office, no employees, no Samoa bank account and no actual warehousing capacity while claiming the 0% offshore exemption on high-volume storage fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation of the income as Samoan-source, withdrawal of tax-exempt IC status, an ESR penalty of up to WST 50,000, compulsory deregistration, and reporting of the beneficial owner to foreign tax authorities under the Exchange of Information framework (CRS/MLI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the arrangement is a sham, the corporate veil is pierced. Directors are personally assessed on the re-characterised income, subject to a five-year director disqualification, asset freezing orders, and criminal conviction for defeating the Revenue where nominee or trustee structures conceal the true controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence on foreign cargo beneficial owners, acceptance of cash payments for storage above the regulatory threshold, or failure to file a suspicious transaction report with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit where the depot is used for sanctions-evasion trade patterns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to WST 500,000 per violation under the Samoa Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018. The AML Supervisory Unit may suspend the statutory licence required for bonded depot operations, order immediate closure, and cause confiscation of funds connected to the suspicious transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and registered agents face personal fines up to WST 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years where they knowingly or with gross negligence permitted the unflagged transaction. The FIU may also seek personal restraint orders on director bank accounts pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the inter-company storage tariff charged to the foreign parent below arm's length to shift taxable profit to the zero-rate FTZ company, or accepting related-party loans from tax havens at excessive interest without an approved WHT reduction certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: MoR adjustment to the arm's length price, a shortfall penalty of 100% of the additional tax, monthly compounding interest, and loss of treaty relief where the WHT-DTA-15 declaration was obtained on false premises. The adjustment may escalate to the 200% fraud penalty if the mispricing is deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed defective transfer pricing documentation are jointly liable for the tax adjustment and penalties. The Samoan courts may issue a charging order on personal property and a prohibition on leaving Samoa while the additional tax and penalties remain unpaid.
